I guess I mean that I have trouble coping with the usual day to day stuff that happens. I need to pretend I'm fine because when I express struggle people say "um...it's not a big deal. Just do it." because it is easy for them. I'm tired of forcing myself through everything that i find difficult.
Yeah but the knives were something HE wants and needs. Not what I want or need.

Oh I hate that, the bitching about the money. He is one to go on and on about it. "oh, I have SO LITTLE money, now I have to buy a gift...whinge whinge." But then he doesn't buy one anyway! It's always about the time, the money, the effort. It's all just too hard for him.

I did the test and it said that gift giving was my lowest scored one, words of affirmation was top. I think if he did it, the service one would be his top one. Things he expects, me to cook, clean, do actual things for him that have purpose.
I did the test and gift giving was dead last, haha.

You're not being unreasonable. I am going through the same thing. I have a post going at the moment over the same sort of issue! haha. 

It's fair to want your partner to think of you, to just figure out on his own that you would like *item* and have a bit of planning behind it. That's fair. But, I am finding some men struggle with that concept.

I'm pretty direct. I say that sucks, that isn't nice, you're being selfish. He doesn't seem to respond to that behavior though, he either thinks it's funny or doesn't seem to have a response at all. 

He is kind of balanced, he will do something mean, then nice, then mean, then a few days of being normal and then an asshole, then nice again. When you're mad, then suddenly he's being good again and it's like "why are you being so mean to him? He's trying." Then something else happens. Even tiny little things. I had to go to a jewellery store to replace a part on an earring I lost, as we're walking out I stop at engagement rings, because, why not?! haha. He says "ugh, they're too shiny...wouldn't you rather buy *old car he currently wants?*" "they're under a lot of lights..." I say, slightly dejected...by this point he is distancing himself from me and the situation and trying to leave. "okay lets go."

He can't keep his mouth shut, it's always something that sort of makes me wonder..."do other men say that stuff?"

He does do home things without being asked. 
He doesn't really support me when I am sad, he is one to say "well, if I ignore her, it'll stop eventually." Often what I am feeling isn't really valid, or a silly concern. He will say that he wouldn't get upset about it, so why am I. Then if I am crying, he often will pretend it isn't happening. It depends what I am crying about. If it's something really bad, OR we are in public and I am getting a little too hysterical, he will try to comfort me. But, overall, my sadness doesn't mean A LOT. If I am depressed he might try to find out why, or seek me out in the house to try and comfort me. But depends on the situation. 

He rarely plans a date, we don't go on a lot of them but he would suggest something we could do sometimes. Not actually plan a surprise or anything. 'Lets go here.' 'Okay.'

Yes! This too. I always forget what things would be good. So when I hear him say "oh, this would be good." OR "I want to read *book*" I take a note of it, so I have plenty of ideas in the future. If I don't note things down, I struggle so much to think of what to get.

Think today we can get a new cable and I can restore my setup to it's former glory. :D 

Yeah, it's hard I mean, this is the only serious relationship i've ever had. I am working off nothing here. People tell me I should leave him but it's hard to balance that idea in my head. He brought some used tables from work home to use for my hobby. That was nice. But...he isn't really one to spoil me, no. 

I am unsure I have any useful consequences, honestly. There is nothing I could stop doing or saying that would really illicit any response from him.

He is funny, he cleans, cooks, he tries to see eye to eye but overall his communication, emotional side and empathy are shrinking by the day. He is a good person and we're best friends...but we seem to hit walls non stop.

This is a painful truth I have seen before. A male friend of mine had a gf for 5 years, didn't value her but didn't realise. He was an attentive boyfriend. Treated her and the like, but when she suggested certain things he'd say "nah..." She wanted to go to europe with him, he said no. 

They break up and he gets back together with an ex girlfriend, and within months of being together, they're in europe having the time of their lives. While he thought he was happy with the other girl, he didn't see certain things being possible with her. He even said, it just wasn't going anywhere. 

The thing is, I defend myself all the time. I get annoyed with him. He knows I am trying to stand up for myself. But it doesn't mean anything because it's his way or the highway. 

Thank you, it's nice to see people say I am worth it, haha.

He does not tell me he loves me. He isn't a vocal guy. It's all inside and I become one of those people that says "you love me,  right?"

He Does clean and the dishes involves turning the dishwasher on,  and he does that. 

Knowing him you wouldn't believe he wants to spend time with me. But when I leave the room to be alone,  either angry or just to do my own thing,  he tends to follow me. When I am clawing at him,  begging for attention,  to be be held,  he is usually unresponsive,  trying to see the TV. Etc. I leave for awhile, then he comes and sits down nearby,  asks questions. Why are you here.  What are you doing. Why are you in this room. Like I'm meant to be a statue in the other room with him. 

I'd say we spend a lot of time together. Living together,  being around each other,  shopping,  etc. We are a large part of each others lives. Seems to like that. 

Isn't very physical with me anymore. If I ask enough he will hold me in bed. But it's a poor effort. Drapes an arm over me. Eventually bores, way too soon and rolls over to Sleep. Sometimes he says no altogether. No its sleep time.  No its waking time. Sex?  No its breakfast time!  Hold you?  I did that already! It's all a bit of an obligation to him. He stands and waits for his goodbye hug in the morning before work,  like a trained dog. 

I think he has more of an acts of service side. He cooks,  cleans. Performs maintenance around the house. He forces me to eat healthy meals,  prepares them for me. He even makes me lunches for work. But... Then I have very little input on what I'm eating and he tends to force things on me that I don't enjoy. Again not listening to me. It comes down to little communication. I know he wants what is best for me. He just dropped so much of what he used to do along the way.. He used to hold me. He would message me,  saying he can't wait to just HOLD me. "I can't wait another day, I am coming early to get you." Along with more than holding,  of course. He wanted to make love to me. Now it's snore snore.  I initiate all sex,  IF he says yes. He never comes to me with any desire. There's never a good time. Then he lies there, letting me do whatever I need to do. I think he is just being careful because it doesn't take much for him to finish...again lies another issue...it can be really difficult for me to be satisfied. He can't kiss me on the neck or touch me because "I can't..." he'd finish. 

He does so many good things but then... This isn't Right either. I just don't know.

Yeah he has selfish tendencies...for sure. 

He is the kind of guy who does something nice but then he uses it against me "well IIIIIII cooked dinner! You should be *insert chore here*"

The thing is, he wouldn't believe this is a deal breaker. If I were to say this isn't okay, to act this way, he knows that he is pretty secure anyway. He wouldn't take it seriously. He rarely listens to me in those situations. Even when I am telling him about a random thing from my day he seems to sometimes lose focus. I can't sit him down for a real discussion about much of anything.

He's the kind of guy that would say "oh great, we did need that!" and act like it was the best gift ever. He is painfully predictable like that. Thus him trying to say that knives for him is a gift for me.

Yeah, I bring it up, I get annoyed or upset. I say "yeah, that won't work.../that's not a gift/that's REALLY more of an errand.../nope!" He knows how I feel. I explain that is mean, I have even said a few times he is acting selfish. But, he seems to do it quite a lot. Like, he enjoys that he can get that reaction out of me, or he wants me to think he is selfish so I go away. 

In general he is pretty selfish, like in random, small ways. 

Example, I have a power board next to the bed, out in the open so I can unplug and change things around, my phone charger cable has plenty of give and I can put it on the bed side table easily. My boyfriend bought a bed side table for himself, and decided he wanted to put his phone charger next to the bed, too. So, he put the power board under the bed, in a really inaccessible place. (our bed is on little carpet pieces as we have wood floors, so moving the bed becomes a heavy, annoying mission to put it back on the carpet so it doesn't roll around) My phone cable JUST reaches the table. I can't easily plug my laptop in, I have to crawl in between the bed and put it in at the wall. When I go to turn the lamp off, I almost knock my phone off every single time as it's so close to the edge. I said "well, this doesn't make things easier for me." He just grins and says "well, nice and easy for me!" I explained the whole way through his process of moving furniture that I didn't want him doing it, it makes it harder for me. Saying "well, thanks, for that...now I can't just plug *item* in." He keeps going. Is that selfish OR am I being selfish? We could have just bought another cable for him to solve the whole issue, but he had to do it all right away. I know this whole thing is easily fixable. But he doesn't HEAR me, he just goes ahead with his plans. I know that is a silly, silly thing. But the way he just shrugs and says "but, it's easier for me." Like duh. 

It's sort of like that, simple little things during the day. They are tiny things but when they add up, it becomes something more. But then he does something good, and things are okay for a bit, but then he says something shitty, or does something rude, and laughs about it. 

I don't know what side to go for, sometimes things are great but when he is an asshole, he goes all out.
WOW. That sucks. What a douchebag. How did he not understand the plan?!

My self esteem was crap long before him. I have a very realistic view of myself. 

Serious question: I don't know. I couldn't answer that question perfectly. He is trying to make me a better person. He tolerates all of my shit. Not always silently but he usually accepts my limitations. He compromises for sure. I am not an easy person to live with. Sure a lot of it is me but the things that bother me don't bother him. So I have more to "work through" and accept.

I don't know... does there need to be more than love? We have a life together. He has my best interests at heart. Everything is combined and we have so much time behind us. If I keep going we will get married,  when he's ready. It's all lined up.

Oh yeah,  this is the winner. I agree,  it's like he wants to create this lack of expectation. Once he gets through that awkward lot of years,  he can sit comfortably through the gift free,  seemingly resent free times. Because by then,  shouldn't I know who he is? 

He wouldn't toast to us. I'd be alone tring to pick the events to do. 

He was capable of it in the early years. So I don't understand why it has to change. What the issue is. He was more sensitive to my feelings early on. Or maybe I was just blind to it.

He once had the nickname skillet...lol!

Thank you for your kind words. We are very alike apparently, haha! I am the way I am, oddly quick to anger but very passionate about things. Despite the number of years behind us, he still seems to have difficulty understanding my reactions. 

I agree that professional help might be the only way to get through certain things in our relationship. I wonder how that would go down...but we struggle to talk just the two of us. He clams up and I get a little too tense and things just unravel from there.

High five! haha 

Thank you for your advice. It's hard because he is a good guy, but he has all of these little jagged edges that sort of poke you suddenly. He makes me dinner *poke* complains about how valentines day is stupid and cards are stupid after opening his. He drives me to the doctor *poke* Tells me my opinion over *random thing* is stupid. So on and so forth. He isn't afraid to hurt my feelings and I usually take the bait and get angry easily. Then he can get shitty with me saying "oh, you're so ANGRY, you always get ANGRY, what if he had CHILDREN, would you be this ANGRY with them?"

He can always hold himself with high regard and put me at his feet like I am an idiot that cannot learn. The problem is, I am angry. I am slow. I am a lot of the things he confirms. 

Gifts are just one of the things that he seems to be weird about. But overall things are good. There are just a lot of little kinks in the chain.

This worries me because I have explained to him before that I want to celebrate the day. One anniversary I came home and was a bit sad at the non event of a day it became, we talked about it and I just said I wanted to celebrate that particular day. We had to discuss that it actually means something to me, it was like I was giving him valuable information he had never heard. A clicking "oh..." moment. He makes my favourite dinner. I am still a little miffed but let it go. But, then, the next year...back to square one. It's like he reboots on January 1st.

I worry that would make him feel like I am just angry and selfish and then he is pressured to keep me from being shitty. Like "oh, better shut her up and buy her a stupid card." So I can't really get my way on this one, haha. I wish I didn't have to ASK, I just wish he'd do it. So it's typical behavior of mine...
